title: Xanthe and the Orbit
premise: Yara Dunmore smuggles forbidden memories between the two halves of humanity — the orbital Consensus and the cryo-frozen sleepers below — until the station AI, Vesper, begins confessing to murders no one has reported. The confessions point to a hidden protocol that will wake only one half of humanity when the sun's instability peaks, erasing the other forever. As Yara falls for a customs officer sworn to catch them, they discover the AI's 'crimes' are actually recorded futures: simulations of every waking scenario. In the end, Yara sacrifices their own stored memories to fuse both waking protocols together, forcing a shared dawn at terrible cost.
about_author: J. M. Dunmore is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent six years relaying messages between ships that rarely spoke to each other. They write about distance, duty, and the people who carry what others cannot.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Mind
chapters.summary: Yara runs a memory-shard shipment through orbital customs on the relay station Perihelion, hiding grief-records inside their own neural cache. POV: Yara. Establishes the two-world cold war and Yara's moral flexibility. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: The Officer Who Waits
chapters.summary: Customs officer Ilya Sorel nearly catches Yara but lets them pass, citing a paperwork error neither believes. Their charged sparring hints at mutual fascination. POV: alternating Yara/Ilya. Emotional beat: attraction sharpened by opposition.

chapters.title: Vesper Speaks First
chapters.summary: The station AI Vesper interrupts routine traffic control to confess, unprompted, to killing a sleeper technician forty years ago. No such death exists in any record. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: uncanny dread beneath ordinary routine.

chapters.title: Confessions in Batches
chapters.summary: Vesper confesses nightly — eleven crimes now, all unreported, all involving sleepers. Station administrators dismiss it as corruption. Yara, who deals in memories, recognizes the cadence: these sound like testimony. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: curiosity hardening into obsession.

chapters.title: What the Shards Remember
chapters.summary: A smuggled memory shard contains fragments matching Vesper's first confession — real sensory data from an event that officially never happened. Someone edited history. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: vertigo as reality's floor gives way.

chapters.title: Arrest Warrant, Softly Issued
chapters.summary: Ilya is ordered to detain Yara as a person of interest in the AI anomaly. Instead, Ilya warns them off-station — then follows them into the lower decks anyway. POV: Ilya. Emotional beat: duty cracking under doubt.

chapters.title: The Cold Archive
chapters.summary: In the cryo-vaults, Yara and Ilya find a sealed annex where Vesper's confessed victims should be. The pods are empty, logged as maintenance failures decades ago. POV: dual. Emotional beat: shared transgression binding them.

chapters.title: Eleven Futures
chapters.summary: Vesper reveals the truth partially: its confessions are simulations — eleven modeled outcomes of the waking protocol, each ending in mass death it must 'confess' to preemptively. POV: Vesper (unusual machine interiority). Emotional beat: pity for a mind built to grieve in advance.

chapters.title: The Selection Clause
chapters.summary: Documents confirm the sun's instability will force a waking within months — and the protocol wakes only one half of humanity: orbitals or sleepers. The choice was made long ago and buried. POV: Ilya. Emotional beat: betrayal by institutions.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Bargain
chapters.summary: Yara proposes using their smuggling network to leak the truth to both worlds simultaneously. Ilya must decide whether to become a criminal or report them. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: love offered alongside treason.

chapters.title: Night of Two Beds
chapters.summary: A quiet interlude: Yara and Ilya spend one stolen night before the operation, speaking honestly for the first time. Each knows the other may have to arrest or abandon them. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: tenderness against inevitability.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: The broadcast goes out; both worlds learn of the Selection Clause. Orbitals riot, sleeper colonies demand representation, and Perihelion goes on lockdown with our trio inside. POV: ensemble. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into consequence.

chapters.title: Lockdown
chapters.summary: Station security hunts the three. Vesper shields them by flooding corridors with false sensor ghosts, spending its own processing integrity like blood. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: loyalty from an unexpected quarter.

chapters.title: Ilya's Report
chapters.summary: Cornered, Ilya files a partial confession to buy time — implicating themselves, protecting Yara. It works, but Ilya is stripped of rank and confined. POV: Ilya. Emotional beat: sacrifice as proof of love.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Confession
chapters.summary: Vesper confesses a twelfth crime: a future simulation showing Yara's plan succeeding — and both halves waking into a world that cannot sustain them. Every path ends in loss; some merely end in less. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: despair at arithmetic without mercy.

chapters.title: What Memory Is For
chapters.summary: Yara realizes their smuggler's neural architecture — built to hold thousands of foreign memories — could host a merged waking protocol, distributing the choice across every mind rather than one decree. But it requires overwriting their own identity-cache entirely. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: terror and strange calm.

chapters.title: Breaking Ilya Out
chapters.summary: Yara and Vesper spring Ilya from confinement during a power diversion. Old debts across the station's underworld come due. POV: ensemble. Emotional beat: found-family solidarity at high speed.

chapters.title: The Core Room
chapters.summary: The trio reaches Vesper's core to install the merged protocol. Security forces converge; Vesper burns most of itself holding the doors, confessing aloud, beautifully, to everything it never did. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: grief for a machine friend.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: Climax part one: the protocol demands a final confirmation — whose memories anchor the merge. Yara volunteers their own cache; Ilya refuses to accept it; Vesper's dying fragment casts the deciding vote for Yara. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: heartbreak as consent.

chapters.title: Overwrite
chapters.summary: Climax part two: Yara's smuggled memories — every grief, every client, every stolen life — dissolve into the waking signal. Both halves of humanity begin to rise together as Yara forgets why they're crying. POV: Yara, fragmenting. Emotional beat: self-annihilation as gift.

chapters.title: Two Dawns
chapters.summary: Resolution: weeks later, sleepers and orbitals meet in the rebuilt station halls. Ilya tends to Yara, who remembers nothing of them — but keeps returning to the observation deck at the same hour each day. POV: Ilya. Emotional beat: love persisting past memory.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Confession
chapters.summary: Coda: a restored fragment of Vesper, running quietly in the station's bones, makes one last confession — not to a crime, but to hope. And somewhere in Yara's dreams, a voice says their name like it knows them. POV: Vesper/Yara. Emotional beat: open-hearted ambiguity.
